subject: Preserve EU request logs for short-term root-cause analysis
messages:
From: Jamie Clarke <jamie.clarke@finserv.co>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@finserv.co>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request to preserve EU request logs for root cause analysis

Hi Vanessa,

We had a production anomaly this morning where a subset of requests from our EU tenant (eu-west-1) returned 502s between 07:05 and 07:18 UTC. Our engineering team is seeing intermittent reproductions and needs a short-term retention carveout to pull the request/response logs and KV cache snapshots for root-cause analysis.

What we're asking for: a read-only preserve of request logs and trace metadata for the EU tenant for the window 2028-07-25T07:00:00Z to 2028-07-25T08:00:00Z (approx), for up to 72 hours. We'll share a minimal sample (attached) and a justification doc. We only require access by two named FinServ engineers; no broad export.

Attached: finserv-incident-log-sample.json, retention-justification.pdf

Can you confirm whether Redwood can temporarily suspend deletion for that slice and provide a scoped access token / audit trail? If there are template forms or legal approvals needed, please let me know and I can route them immediately.

Thanks,
Jamie Clarke
Sr SRE, FinServ Capital
jamie.clarke@finserv.co

---
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Clarke <jamie.clarke@finserv.co>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Request to preserve EU request logs for root cause analysis

Marcus / Rachel — forwarding an urgent customer request from FinServ. They want a short timebox (about an hour) of EU request logs and KV cache snapshots preserved for up to 72 hours for RCA. They explicitly ask for read-only access for two customer engineers.

Quick context: this is a high-value customer (FIN-4921) and they're in an onboarding phase for dedicated capacity. They flagged this as blocking a P0 investigation. We need to answer:
- Is a timeboxed retention exception feasible in eu-west-1?
- What controls can we apply (access gating, audit logs, encryption, no export)?
- Do we need legal sign-off / DocuSign?

I'm happy to coordinate communications with the customer's legal team if necessary. Marcus — can infra provide the minimal snapshot and a scoped, ephemeral read token? Rachel — can security approve the exception if we satisfy the controls?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: access-request-form.docx (filled by Jamie)

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, rachel.kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Clarke <jamie.clarke@finserv.co>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request to preserve EU request logs for root cause analysis

Vanessa — we can support a very narrow, auditable exception provided we implement the following constraints: 

1) Time window: persist only the exact shard/time range requested (07:00–08:00 UTC) and automatically re-enable normal deletion after 72 hours.
2) Region-local: snapshots must remain in eu-west-1 and not be copied to other regions.
3) Access: issue a scoped, one-time read token valid for a maximum of 48 hours to two principal IDs (we will need their Redwood user emails). No bulk export APIs; access will be read-only via a temporary console view or S3-like signed URL with download disabled.
4) Audit: every access will be logged; we will produce a signed audit bundle (audit-trail.csv) showing who accessed what and when.
5) Encryption & retention flag: mark snapshot with ephemeral retention override tag and HSM-wrapped key.

Action items for FinServ: confirm the two engineer identities (full emails) and sign the access-request-form (they attached a draft — we'll need legal countersign). For Redwood: I will stage the snapshot in a locked bucket and coordinate with Security for sign-off.

Estimate: I can have the snapshot staged within ~3 hours after legal sign-off and identity confirmation.

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime Infrastructure
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
LinkedIn: /marcuslin

---
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Clarke <jamie.clarke@finserv.co>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request to preserve EU request logs for root cause analysis — Security sign-off (conditional)

Thanks for the context. Security will approve a short-term, region-scoped retention exception under these mandatory conditions: 

- Narrow scope: only the EU tenant request logs and specified KV cache keys between 07:00–08:00 UTC on 2028-07-25. No additional data slices.
- Duration: maximum 72 hours of retention override, after which normal data lifecycle rules will re-apply automatically.
- Access controls: scoped token for exactly two identities, MFA required, access window limited to 48 hours.
- No export/no copy: data must remain in eu-west-1 and be accessible only through the temporary read interface; bulk downloads disabled.
- Legal acknowledgement: FinServ must return the signed access-request-form and legal@finserv.co must ACK the controls.
- Audit & attest: Redwood will produce an audit bundle and an attestation email when the data is purged.

If FinServ agrees, Marcus proceed to stage the snapshot and I'll confirm encryption/key handling with our KMS team. Vanessa — please share the two engineer emails and the signed form when available; loop in Redwood Legal if there are any unusual contract terms.

Approved (conditional): Rachel Kim
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
